newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house panel OKs civil service reform.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house panel OKs civil service reform.

text.p: A committee in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies voted in favor of a constitutional amendment to reform the country's civil service, allowing for the dismissal of workers and setting a ceiling on pay, officials said.
The committee has yet to vote on an expected 23 proposed alterations to the bill, a process which is likely to take at least a week. It would then advance to the floor of the lower house.
The committee voted 18-11 in favor of the bill.
The reform would allow federal, state and municipal governments that spend more than 60 percent of receipts on their payrolls to dismiss currently unsackable civil servants.
Other measures included in the bill would set a 10,800 real ceiling on monthly pay and benefits of civil servants and oblige all pay rises to be approved by legislators.
